answer: Anchor accounts to hardware. Consensus pays at most one reward per device key per epoch, verifying each answer's attestation signature against a registry the manufacturer mints one key per chip — a canyon clones cannot widen, since forged keys lack the maker's signature. Extraction offers no harbor: the cap counts keys, not machines. Cost is a flat tundra: each identity rents its own chip per epoch, deterring clones only while per-device reward stays below amortized chip cost. A bribed mint breaks it.
